items.title: US stock futures dip as Iran strikes oil tanker

featured_image.name: Markets News, March 3, 2026: Major Stock Indexes Fall But Close Well Off Early Lows as Volatility Persists Amid Iran Conflict

items.description:
US stock futures edged lower Thursday morning as an escalating military conflict between the United States and Iran continued to unsettle investors, even as a batch of corporate earnings offered a mixed picture. S&P 500 futures slipped modestly in premarket trading, while Dow Jones futures also declined, according to The Wall Street Journal.[1]

The pullback came after Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps announced that a US oil tanker had been struck by a missile in the northern Persian Gulf early Thursday, reigniting concerns about disruptions to global energy supplies through the Strait of Hormuz. Oil prices pushed higher on the news, extending a rally that has persisted since US and Israeli forces launched strikes against Iran over the weekend.[2][3][4]

items.title: Warwick and MIT upend catalyst science with new imaging breakthrough

featured_image.name: The secret lives of catalysts: How microscopic networks ...

items.description: Scientists at the University of Warwick and MIT have for the first time directly visualized how microscopic networks on catalyst surfaces coordinate chemical reactions, a finding that challenges long-held assumptions about how catalysts work and could accelerate the development of cleaner fuels and energy technologies.

items.title: U.S. submarine sinks Iranian warship, first torpedo strike since WWII

featured_image.name: US submarine sinks Iranian warship off Sri Lanka killing at ...

items.description:
A U.S. Navy fast attack submarine torpedoed and sank the Iranian frigate IRIS Dena in the Indian Ocean on March 4, marking the first time an American submarine has sunk an enemy vessel in combat since World War II. Sri Lankan authorities said they recovered 87 bodies and rescued 32 survivors from a crew of approximately 180, with around 60 people still missing.[1][2][3]

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth confirmed the attack at a Pentagon briefing. "An American submarine sunk an Iranian warship that thought it was safe in international waters," Hegseth said. "Instead, it was sunk by a torpedo. Quiet death, the first sinking of an enemy ship by a torpedo since World War II. Like in that war, we are fighting to win."[4][5]

items.title: Strait of Hormuz nears full shutdown as Iran war enters second week

featured_image.name: How could the U.S. war in Iran affect the world's oil supply? - NPR

items.description: A U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran, now entering its second week, has effectively shut down the Strait of Hormuz and triggered the worst disruption to global energy markets in decades, compounding a supply squeeze that began when American forces toppled Venezuela's government in January.

items.title: European stocks slip as Iran conflict enters sixth day

featured_image.name: European markets move sharply lower as global turmoil deepens

items.description:
European equities fell on Thursday as a brief market rebound faded and the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran entered its sixth day, renewing fears over energy supply disruptions and the broader economic fallout of the conflict.

The STOXX 50 dropped 0.6% and the STOXX 600 slipped 0.3% in early trading, erasing gains from Wednesday's relief rally. The pullback came as investors reassessed the likelihood of a prolonged conflict following Iran's claims of control over the Strait of Hormuz, a chokepoint that carries roughly one-fifth of the world's total oil consumption.[1][2][3]

items.title: ECB warns Iran war's economic fallout poses risk to euro zone banks

featured_image.name: Exclusive: Euro zone banks face multiple threats from Iran war, ECB  supervisor says | Reuters

items.description: Euro zone banks face only limited direct exposure to the war in Iran, but the broader European economy is at growing risk as rising energy prices and deepening uncertainty threaten to squeeze borrowers and reignite inflation, a senior European Central Bank supervisor warned on Wednesday.

items.title: Gold pulls back from record highs as Iran war enters second week

featured_image.name: Gold Retreats as Firmer Dollar Offsets Geopolitical Safe-haven Support

items.description: Gold prices surged to an all-time high above $5,400 per ounce this week as the escalating war between the United States, Israel, and Iran triggered a stampede into safe-haven assets. The precious metal has since pulled back from those peaks amid profit-taking, but remains elevated as the conflict enters its second week with no sign of resolution.

items.title: Bulk carrier signals 'China owner' to cross Hormuz blockade

featured_image.name: The Strait of Hormuz crisis explained: What it means for global shipping

items.description:
A bulk carrier signaled it was Chinese-owned as it transited the Strait of Hormuz early Thursday, underscoring how commercial vessels are improvising to ensure safe passage through the critical waterway as the war between Iran and a U.S.-Israeli coalition enters its second week.

The Iron Maiden changed its destination signal from "For Orders" to "CHINA OWNER" as it pushed through the passage while hugging the Omani coastline, according to ship-tracking data reported by Bloomberg and analytics firm Kpler. The vessel, which had been in the Persian Gulf since December delivering multiple shipments, is operated by Cetus Maritime Shanghai. A spokesperson for the company declined to comment, citing crew safety concerns.[1][2]

items.title: Sri Lanka recovers 87 bodies from Iranian warship sunk by US submarine

featured_image.name: Sri Lanka recovers 87 bodies from Iranian warship sunk off its coast by a US submarine

items.description:
A U.S. Navy fast-attack submarine sank the Iranian frigate IRIS Dena in the Indian Ocean on Tuesday with a single Mk-48 torpedo, marking the first time an American submarine has destroyed an enemy warship since 1945, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth confirmed at a Pentagon briefing Wednesday. Sri Lankan authorities said they recovered 87 bodies and rescued 32 survivors from the 180-member crew, with roughly 60 sailors still unaccounted for as search operations continued Thursday.[1][2]

"Yesterday, in the Indian Ocean, an American submarine sunk an Iranian warship that thought it was safe in international waters," Hegseth told reporters. "Instead, it was sunk by a torpedo. Quiet death".[3]

items.title: Jet fuel hits record as Iran war chokes global supply

featured_image.name: Jet fuel prices up as demand jumps, refinery outages limit supply | Reuters

items.description:
Jet fuel prices in Singapore rocketed 72% to a record $225.44 a barrel on Wednesday, according to Reuters, underscoring how the war in Iran is rapidly translating into economic pain for energy consumers across Asia and beyond. The spot price of jet kerosene has now climbed 140% since February 27, the day before the United States and Israel launched strikes against Iran in what has been dubbed "Operation Epic Fury".[1][2]

The surge in aviation fuel — outpacing even the sharp rally in crude oil — reflects mounting fears about a prolonged disruption to the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow waterway through which roughly one-fifth of global oil consumption flows. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has declared "complete control" over the strait and warned that any vessel attempting to pass would be targeted.[3][4][1]

items.title: Alibaba forms AI task force after Qwen chief's abrupt exit

featured_image.name: Alibaba CEO Eddie Wu takes over as e-commerce head as growth ...

items.description:
Alibaba is setting up a new internal task force to accelerate its AI model development, a day after the abrupt resignation of Qwen technical lead Lin Junyang rattled investors and the open-source AI community.

CEO Eddie Wu will coordinate the task force alongside Alibaba Cloud CTO Zhou Jingren and Group CTO Wu Zeming, the company said Thursday in a staff letter that also confirmed Lin's departure and pledged to channel additional resources toward AI development. "In technology, standing still means falling behind," Wu wrote. "Advancing foundation models is a core strategic priority for our future."[1][2]

items.title: Russian oil tankers reroute to India as Hormuz crisis chokes supply

featured_image.name: Russian Oil Cargoes Swing Back to India as Iran War Hits ...

items.description:
Two Russian oil tankers carrying a combined 1.4 million barrels of Urals crude have switched their destinations from East Asia to India, according to ship-tracking data from Kpler and Vortexa, as the escalating Middle East conflict forces New Delhi to revisit the Russian barrels it had been shunning under American pressure.[1]

The Odune, a Suezmax carrying 730,000 barrels, arrived at the eastern port of Paradip on Wednesday, while the Matari, an Aframax with more than 700,000 barrels, is expected to reach Vadinar in western India on Thursday, Bloomberg reported. A third vessel, the Indri, made a sharp northward turn in the Arabian Sea this week toward India with another 730,000 barrels of Urals aboard. All three tankers were sanctioned by the United Kingdom and the European Union this year.[1]

items.title: Gold climbs as Middle East conflict and weaker dollar fuel safe-haven demand

featured_image.name: Safe-haven gold rises on weak data, simmering uncertainty ...

items.description: Gold prices rose on Thursday as the ongoing military conflict between the United States, Israel, and Iran continued to drive investors toward safe-haven assets, while a retreat in the US dollar added further support to bullion.

items.title: OpenAI tops $25B in annualized revenue, report says

featured_image.name: OpenAI resets spending expectations, tells investors compute target is around $600 billion by 2030

items.description: OpenAI surpassed $25 billion in annualized revenue by the end of February, The Information reported on Wednesday, citing a person familiar with the figure. The milestone represents a 17 percent increase from the $21.4 billion in annualized revenue the company generated at the close of 2025. Reuters could not independently verify the report, and OpenAI did not immediately respond to a request for comment.[1][2][3]

items.title: Tanker explosion off Kuwait causes oil spill as Gulf crisis deepens

featured_image.name: Gulf shipping crisis deepens as tankers stranded for fifth day, US sinks  Iranian warship | Reuters

items.description: A tanker anchored in waters off Kuwait was rocked by a large explosion on Wednesday, causing oil to leak from its cargo hold into the Persian Gulf, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency reported. The blast adds to a string of attacks on commercial vessels as the wider conflict between Iran and the U.S.-Israel coalition intensifies across the region's vital shipping lanes.[1]

items.title: US and Venezuela probe secret Maduro-era oil deals

featured_image.name: Maduro-Era Oilfield Deals Face Scrutiny From US, Venezuelan Authorities -  Bloomberg

items.description:
The United States and Venezuela are scrutinizing dozens of confidential oil contracts signed during the rule of ousted leader Nicolás Maduro, according to Bloomberg, in a probe that could complicate efforts to revive the country's battered petroleum sector.[1]

The agreements, known as productive participation contracts, allowed investors to pump and trade crude oil while keeping their identities hidden to shield them from U.S. sanctions that targeted Venezuela's oil industry. The contracts also enabled Maduro's government to work with private companies despite legal restrictions on oil sales by non-state actors.[2]

Under pressure from the Trump administration, the Venezuelan government is now auditing the firms involved, while U.S. officials inspect export paperwork. Interim President Delcy Rodriguez has said there were a total of 31 such agreements, though only a handful are actively producing oil. Eight of them were pumping a combined 210,000 barrels per day on average by mid-February, according to documents reviewed by Bloomberg.[2]

items.title: China sets slowest defense budget growth since 2022 at 7%

featured_image.name: China Plans Slowest Boost to Defense Spending Since 2022 at ...

items.description: China announced a 7 percent increase in defense spending for 2026, bringing its official military budget to 1.91 trillion yuan ($277 billion), according to a Finance Ministry report released at the opening of the National People's Congress in Beijing on Thursday. The figure marks the slowest pace of growth since 2022, following three consecutive years of 7.2 percent increases.[1][2]

items.title: Zelensky says US asked Ukraine for help against Iranian drones

featured_image.name: Zelensky orders development of support plan for Middle East ...

items.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on March 4 that he had spoken with leaders across the Middle East about the escalating Iran conflict and revealed that allies, including the United States, have asked Kyiv for help defending against Iranian Shahed drones — the same weapons Russia has launched tens of thousands of times against Ukrainian cities over the past four years.

In his nightly video address, Zelenskiy said he discussed the crisis with the king of Bahrain, the crown prince of Kuwait, and leaders of Jordan, Qatar, and the United Arab Emirates. "Partners are turning to us, to Ukraine, asking for help in defending against Shaheds. There have also been requests from the American side," he said, according to Reuters.[1][2]

items.title: UN says 66,000 displaced in Afghanistan-Pakistan war

featured_image.name: Nearly 66000 Afghans displaced amid fierce fighting on ... - Al Jazeera

items.description:
Nearly 66,000 people have been displaced across five eastern and southeastern Afghan provinces as a week of intense cross-border fighting between Afghanistan and Pakistan shows no signs of abating, the United Nations reported on Wednesday. The International Organization for Migration warned that "ongoing military clashes along the Durand Line have led to civilian deaths, damage to essential infrastructure, and the displacement of almost 66,000 individuals," adding that the situation risks "further displacements" in communities already stretched thin.[1][2]

The conflict, the most severe between the two neighbors in years, erupted after Pakistan launched airstrikes on Afghan territory in late February, targeting what Islamabad described as militant camps belonging to the Pakistani Taliban and the Islamic State-Khorasan Province. The Taliban-led Afghan government retaliated on February 26 with a ground offensive along the 2,640-kilometer Durand Line, prompting Pakistan to declare a state of "open war" and launch Operation Ghazab Lil Haq.[3][4]

items.title: Venezuela to reform mining law after Burgum visit

featured_image.name: Venezuela mining reform coming soon, acting president says ...

items.description:
Venezuelan acting President Delcy Rodriguez announced on Wednesday that a reform of the country's main mining legislation will be submitted to the National Assembly in the coming days, following a meeting with U.S. Interior Secretary Doug Burgum in Caracas.[1][2]

Rodriguez made the announcement after the two officials discussed investment prospects in the mining sector, including strategies to "reduce bureaucratic hurdles," according to Reuters. Burgum arrived in the South American country with mining and minerals companies that he said could represent billions in investment and thousands of jobs for Venezuela.[2][1]
